issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 4 (th:main_ls) and its consequence Corollary 2 (cor:LS) suffer from multiple interlocking mathematical failures: (1) In both statements, the parameter $p$ appearing in the bound $(m/\log(m/\epsilon))^{ rac{1}{2}- rac{1}{p}}$ and constant $C( m{ho}, p)$ is nowhere introduced, defined, or quantified. (2) The statement of Theorem 4 asserts that a single index set $S$ exists uniformly for all $f$ with holomorphic extension to $\mathcal{E}_{ m{ho}}$, but the proof in Appendix B defines $S$ to be the support of the best $s$-term approximation of $f$, which depends on the unknown target function $f$; this makes $S$ an oracle set that cannot be known a priori to construct the least squares matrix $ m{\Psi}$. (3) For the claimed setting of unweighted least squares with the uniform measure $\varrho$ and the Legendre basis, the sample complexity bound $|S| \leq \lceil m/\log(m/\epsilon) ceil$ (i.e., $m \sim |S| \log(m/\epsilon)$) is mathematically false: the Christoffel function for multivariate Legendre polynomials grows quadratically with degree, meaning unweighted least squares with uniform i.i.d. sampling requires $m \gtrsim |S|^2$, not $m \sim |S| \log m$, to ensure invertibility and stability of $ m{\Psi}^*  m{\Psi}$ with high probability.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Properly quantify $p \in (0, 1]$, restrict the scope by excluding the uniform measure/Legendre basis regime (or worsen the sample complexity for Legendre to quadratic in $|S|$), include the necessary dimension-dependent constant in the Chebyshev sample complexity condition, and either construct a deterministic, a priori index set $S$ depending only on $ m{ho}$ or explicitly formulate the result as an oracle bound for a known best $s$-term support.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical guarantee for least squares polynomial surrogate models (Corollary 2) and its underlying theorem (Theorem 4) are mathematically invalid as stated, leaving the paper's least squares convergence and sample complexity guarantees unsupported.
issues.title: Unsound statement, quantifiers, and sample complexity for least squares polynomial approximation
issues.why_classification: Any mathematically sound resolution requires excluding an advertised regime (unweighted least squares for Legendre polynomials under uniform sampling), materially worsening the sample complexity guarantee, and altering the quantifier structure and definition of the approximation space $S$.
